review.reason: A heterogeneous method chain alternates field_expression and call_expression nodes, so the existing same-type flatten cannot express rustfmt’s dot-by-dot breaks at width 100.
The same heterogeneous chain is not expressible by the existing flatten, and rustfmt additionally inserts a closure block that the linear, non-destructive package cannot synthesize.

Entry 22 plus the established comment entries. Entry 22: comment_cells is package-wide and unscoped, so Rust cannot align list-item comments without also aligning statement comments, which fails gate 2 idempotence on this very file at both widths. Entries 9 and 7 remain the other causes here: a mid-expression block comment cannot be placed by the package, and a rule cannot tell a comment-forced break from a width-forced one.

The remaining method-chain layout is the existing heterogeneous-chain flatten limit, and rustfmt’s broken-arm brace placement depends on ancestor break context unavailable to this rule.

Rustfmt adds a trailing comma to this one-item broken parameter list, but trail intentionally does not synthesize a comma for one item; this is existing FINDINGS 3.
Keeping the long string assignment flat preserves the package’s consistent handling of opaque overlong leaves and avoids a let-level group that regresses the matching sequences corpus.

Entry 22: rustfmt aligns trailing comments on list items only, and comment_cells is a package-wide switch with no scope. Measured three ways: a package-placed cell adds the tabwriter pad AND the suffix comment_gap, so every row is one column too wide; the header never fires on struct fields at all, because tree-sitter-rust makes the separator comma the comment's preceding sibling and comment_cells skips tokens; and where it does fire it aligns statement comments, which fails gate 2 idempotence on comments.rs at both widths (DISQUALIFIED). Scoping comment cells to a cellblock is the missing capability -- with it, widths.rs match arms are byte-identical to rustfmt.
